label: Structured input
summary: Structured input refers to constrained, limited user input in AI interfaces: think buttons, numbered options, and predefined choices rather than open free-text fields. It is the opposite of the conversational, unstructured paradigm that became the default with generative AI. Claude Code's interface choices are a concrete example of structured input making a comeback.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike uses structured input as a lens to reframe something usually seen as regressive — buttons, numbered menus, IVR — as actually a smart design response to two real problems with free-text AI interfaces: usability (people don't know how to prompt well) and security (unconstrained text input opens the door to prompt injection and unintended changes to how a system works). The IVR comparison is deliberate and a little provocative: the thing everyone was glad to leave behind might be exactly what we need again.
open_questions: Where exactly is the right boundary between structured and conversational input in an AI application — is it per use case, per user type, or something else?
How do you design structured input that constrains without frustrating users, given that the whole promise of conversational AI was less friction?
